source_name: Slov-Lex — e-Zbierka (Zbierka zákonov SR), consolidated legal texts
source_subtype: official law gazette / consolidated legislation database
why_relevant: Official, legally binding electronic Collection of Laws of the Slovak Republic. Every banking/payments statute, its amendments and its effective dates (účinnosť) are legally required to appear here, with time-versioned consolidated texts (e.g. Act 483/2001 Z. z. on Banks, Act 492/2009 Z. z. on Payment Services). It is the authoritative anchor for any deadline or in-force date in SK.

source_name: Slov-Lex — static PDF/HTML mirror of the Collection of Laws (static.slov-lex.sk)
why_relevant: Machine-friendly delivery layer for the same official texts: per-act PDFs of the promulgated issue (čiastka) and per-date HTML consolidations. This is the practical ingestion endpoint for an automated pipeline, sidestepping the JS portal.

source_name: Slov-Lex — Medzirezortné pripomienkové konanie (inter-ministerial comment procedure) / Pripomienky
why_relevant: The formal public consultation stage (MPK) with a hard comment deadline. Comments are published with their author — so this exposes which banks, the Slovenská banková asociácia, card schemes, fintechs, NBS and other ministries objected to what, and how the submitter responded (vyhodnotenie pripomienok). Directly serves the 'consultations' and 'deadlines' topics and doubles as an actor map.

source_name: NR SR — Parlamentné tlače (parliamentary prints) index
why_relevant: Canonical repository of every bill text (návrh zákona), explanatory memorandum, committee reports (spoločná správa výborov) and amendments as tabled in the National Council. Required reading to know the final wording and the transitional/effective-date provisions actually voted on.

source_name: NR SR — Návrhy zákonov predložené NR SR / bill detail tracker
why_relevant: Live state machine for each bill: submitter, reading stage, committee assignment, dates, votes and outcome. The per-bill detail page (sid=zakony/zakon&MasterID=<id>) is the natural join key between the Slov-Lex LP process and the final Z. z. number.

source_name: NR SR — Výbor pre financie a rozpočet (Finance and Budget Committee)
why_relevant: The committee that owns banking/payments bills. Its agendas, resolutions and recommended amendments are where late-stage substantive changes (including unrelated 'prílepky' riders attached to banking acts) surface before the final vote. Also an actor map of the MPs who shape financial-sector rules.

source_name: NR SR — Digitálna knižnica (parliamentary digital library)
why_relevant: Structured browser over parliamentary documents by term, session and committee — a more crawlable route into historical prints and committee records than the legacy search forms. Useful for building a back-catalogue of banking-act amendment histories.

source_name: NR SR — Hlasovania (voting records and search)
why_relevant: Confirms the exact date a banking/payments act was adopted (the anchor for computing vacatio legis and effective dates) and shows the coalition/opposition split, which is a weak predictor of durability of a rule across an electoral cycle.

source_name: TV NR SR — parliamentary session video archive
why_relevant: Verbatim debate on banking bills, including ministerial statements about intent and timing that never make it into the written record. Useful for attributing positions to named officials in the actor map; low priority for automated monitoring.

source_name: Úrad vlády SR — Legislatívna rada vlády SR (mandate, membership, legislative rules)
why_relevant: Names the members and working commissions of the Legislative Council and hosts the Legislatívne pravidlá vlády SR plus the government's legislative task plans — the procedural rulebook that determines comment-period lengths and document types you can expect for any draft. Core input to the actor map.

source_name: HSR — Hospodárska a sociálna rada SR (tripartite council) materials
why_relevant: Draft laws with economic impact are reviewed by the tripartite body before Cabinet; its records show employer-side (incl. financial-sector association) objections and can flag delays to a banking bill's timetable.

source_name: Ministerstvo financií SR — Plán legislatívnych úloh / legislatíva section
why_relevant: MF SR is the submitting body for essentially all SK banking and payments legislation. Its published legislative task plan states which acts it intends to amend in which month — a forward calendar that lets you anticipate LP/PI entries before they appear on Slov-Lex.

source_name: NBS — Zoznam platných právnych predpisov vydaných NBS / legislation register
why_relevant: Secondary legislation layer of this cell: NBS decrees (vyhlášky) and measures (opatrenia) are themselves promulgated in the Zbierka zákonov, and NBS maintains the authoritative index linking each measure to its Z. z. number and effective date. Also publishes an English-language mirror of key acts, which is the practical EN entry point for this cell.

source_name: N-Lex (EU) — Slovak national law interface to Slov-Lex
why_relevant: European Commission-maintained gateway describing the Slovak national legal database and offering a multilingual query form over it. Valuable as documentation of the SK database's structure and metadata, and as an English-language route in for non-Slovak-reading analysts.

source_name: slovlex-scraper (open-source Slov-Lex scraper, GitHub)
why_relevant: Community code that already solves Slov-Lex list scraping; a free head start on URL patterns and pagination behaviour for the ingestion layer. Maintenance status and current compatibility with the redesigned portal are unverified.

source_name: data.slovensko.sk — national open data catalogue
why_relevant: Central catalogue where Slovak public bodies are obliged to register open datasets. The place to check whether NR SR, Úrad vlády or MF SR publish machine-readable dumps of bills, votes or legislative processes rather than requiring scraping. Predecessor catalogue data.gov.sk still holds legacy datasets.

source_name: Ekosystém Slovensko.Digital — otvorené dáta (civic data mirrors and APIs)
why_relevant: Civic-tech project that republishes Slovak public-sector datasets as SQL dumps and REST/SQL APIs, often more usable than the originals. Potential shortcut for parliamentary and registry data underpinning the actor map.

source_name: Zákony pre ľudí (zakonypreludi.sk) — commercial consolidated law archive
why_relevant: Widely used unofficial mirror of the Zbierka zákonov with consolidated texts back to 1945, a 'newly promulgated regulations' feed and clean stable URLs (/zz/2001-483). Excellent cross-check and fallback when Slov-Lex rendering fails — but never citable as the legal source of record.

source_name: AUTORA (autora.sk) — time-versioned law texts mirror
why_relevant: Another unofficial mirror exposing per-date consolidated versions via clean URLs (/zz/2009/492/20250117/), useful for diffing a statute across effective dates when Slov-Lex versioning is awkward to navigate.

source_name: ULC Čarnogurský — legislative bulletin (Bulletin ULC)
why_relevant: Slovak law-firm bulletin that narrates each banking-act amendment in plain language with the effective date and the practical obligations — a fast triage layer that tells you which Z. z. number is worth reading in full. Representative of a whole class (law firms, Big Four, SBA) worth systematically enumerating.

source_name: EUR-Lex — National transposition measures (NIM) database
why_relevant: Authoritative, weekly-updated record of which Slovak legal acts Member State authorities notified as transposing each EU directive (CRD, PSD2/PSD3, AMLD/AMLD6, CCD2, NIS2). Single best machine-readable proof of SK transposition status and dates.

source_name: Single Market and Competitiveness Scoreboard — Transposition of Single Market directives
why_relevant: Commission's own measurement of Slovakia's transposition deficit, conformity deficit and delay length. Gives a comparative, dated signal of whether SK is late implementing financial-services directives.

source_name: Single Market Scoreboard — Infringement cases
why_relevant: Tracks open infringement proceedings against Slovakia for late/incorrect transposition — an early warning that a SK implementing act is coming under Commission pressure.

source_name: EBA — Guidelines compliance tables
why_relevant: EBA's own compliance tables state, per guideline, whether Slovakia's competent authority complies / partially complies / intends to comply. Cross-check against NBS's own declarations; PDFs are structured and datable.

source_name: EBA — Interactive Single Rulebook
why_relevant: Article-by-article map from CRR/CRD/PSD2 (and successors) to the RTS/ITS/guidelines that implement them — the fastest way to enumerate the obligation set that will land on SK institutions and to build a deadline inventory.

source_name: EBA — Single Rulebook Q&A
why_relevant: Questions are submitted by named/attributed institutions and authorities per country; SK-origin questions reveal exactly which implementation points Slovak banks and payment institutions find unclear — an indirect read on local compliance friction.

source_name: EBA EUCLID — Payment Institutions Register (PSD2 register)
why_relevant: EU-wide register of authorised payment/e-money institutions and agents, filterable to Slovakia. Under PSD3/PSR the register scope changes; the SK entity list is the base population to which EU deadlines apply.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision — List of supervised entities
why_relevant: Defines, monthly, which Slovak banks are directly ECB-supervised (significant) vs NBS-supervised (less significant, incl. high-impact LSIs). Determines which EU supervisory expectations apply to whom in SK.

source_name: ECB opinions on draft national legislation (CON series) — Slovakia
why_relevant: Slovakia must consult the ECB on draft laws touching currency, means of payment, NBS or financial stability. ECB CON opinions therefore surface SK draft banking/payments legislation before it passes, with EU-law critique attached. Filterable by addressee Member State via EUR-Lex advanced search.
